summary:
Several female Dutch public figures are considering legal action after manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces appeared on a website with 13 million monthly visitors. The victims include artists, TV presenters, Olympic athletes, former ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. The newspaper AD did not name the platform to protect victims. Outgoing justice minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file police reports. Some managers and spokespeople confirmed reports have been filed or legal steps are being considered.

Deepfake pornography is illegal under revenge porn laws. Lawyers advise victims to report it, after which prosecutors can try to shut down the site. Other options include a mass claim, a complaint to the Dutch data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. In a previous case, a 39 year old man from Amersfoort received a suspended 180 hour community service sentence for making deepfake porn of presenter Welmoed Sijtsma.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
